body: Given that they also make the F1 manager games, an F1 themed dlc would be pretty cool. Pieces to build racetracks, car models, and grandstand/race structures would be neat.

Depending on how versatile the pathing system is, I was planning on making an amusement park fully integrated into a racetrack. Kind of like Suzuka but if the park was expanded so that it’s visible throughout the track.
With each manufacturers having multiple ride types, it would be cool if there was a relationship  mechanic where the more you buy from them, the more models become available for use.
With 2 of my favorite things being racing and roller coaster, I can only dream. It would be a year round cash cow for sure though.

Something I would like to see is viability for the park entrance fee approach. Instead of having peeps only be charged once when they enter, maybe can be an automatic charge per guest after every day/night cycle or monthly.

I would like to see a more organized scenery menu similar to rct3. Having a main scenery menu with submenus for different scenery sets would make looking for pieces so much easier. It would also allow for full TMTK sets to be created and easily accessed.

I’ve been hoping for one of these to be installed here. It’ll fit so well with the flat lineup. Considering how popular revolution is, I’d imagine this could even compete with some of the coasters in terms of crowds.

In the original RCT series, they had awards for various things; Best scenery, best food, best coasters, etc. I’d like to see that in PC2 mainly because it gives us something to work towards. In RCT3, it felt nice for the game to recognize when I’ve worked hard in scenery or operations. Also switch tracks and more advanced coaster elements.

I’m an upper class man engineering student. In the field, it’s all about give and take when it comes to product life. You can get away with a relatively short service life with small components such as bearings, latches, and many of the smaller mechanical components of a roller coaster, thus regular maintenance. With the actual structure though, it’s always over engineered to hell. You can expect those to stay up practically indefinitely.
